c: Professional junk removal teams handle the heavy lifting, loading, and hauling.
However, preparing the garage helps the crew quickly identify what needs to be removed.
It can also reduce confusion about which belongings should stay.
A few minutes of preparation can make a major difference when the team arrives.

blocks.text: 11. Move Your Vehicle If Necessary

c: If you normally park inside the garage, move your vehicle outside before the cleanout.
This gives the crew more room to work.
It also protects your vehicle from accidental scratches or damage while large items are being removed.
If the driveway is available, leaving enough space for the junk removal truck can make the process easier.

blocks.text: 14. Don’t Start a Last-Minute Garage Sale

c: A garage cleanout can tempt homeowners to try to sell everything.
But be realistic.
If you’ve had an item sitting unused for years, spending weeks trying to sell it may delay your cleanout.
If something has genuine value, sell it.
For inexpensive items that aren’t worth the time and effort, donation or professional removal may be the more practical option.

blocks.text: 15. Take Care of Items That the Company Cannot Accept

c: Some materials may not be suitable for standard junk removal.
Depending on local regulations and the company’s policies, this may include certain hazardous materials.
Always tell the company what you have before the appointment.
If something isn’t accepted, ask what disposal option is appropriate.
Never mix potentially hazardous materials into a regular junk pile without checking first.

blocks.text: 17. Tell the Crew About Large or Heavy Items

c: Don’t wait until the team arrives to mention that there is a piano, hot tub, commercial freezer, or extremely heavy piece of equipment in the garage.
Tell them beforehand.
Large or heavy items may require additional planning and equipment.

blocks.text: 18. Keep Children and Pets Away From the Work Area

c: Garage cleanouts involve lifting, carrying, and moving large objects.
For safety, keep children and pets away from the garage while the crew is working.
This gives the team more space and reduces the risk of someone getting in the way of heavy items being moved.

blocks.text: How Long Does a Garage Cleanout Take?

c: The time required depends on the size of the garage and the amount of junk.
A small garage with a few unwanted items may be completed relatively quickly.
A garage packed with years of accumulated furniture, boxes, appliances, and equipment can take longer.
The best way to estimate the time is to provide photos and details about the amount of junk before booking.

blocks.text: Frequently Asked Questions

items.title: What should I do before a garage cleanout?
text: Decide what you want to keep, identify the items that need to be removed, separate important belongings, clear small obstacles from walkways, and tell the junk removal team about any large or unusual items.

items.title: Do I need to move everything outside before the junk removal team arrives?
text: No. A full-service junk removal company can typically handle the lifting and loading. You can simply identify which items should be removed.

items.title: Should I organize my garage before junk removal?
text: You don’t need to completely organize it. However, separating items you want to keep from items you want removed can make the cleanout faster and easier.

items.title: How do I prepare large items for garage cleanout?
text: Don’t attempt to move extremely heavy items yourself. Tell the junk removal company about large furniture, appliances, equipment, or other bulky items before the appointment.

items.title: Can junk removal companies recycle garage items?
text: Many companies recycle or donate suitable materials. Live Junk Free prioritizes recycling and donations whenever possible.

items.title: How can I make my garage cleanout faster?
text: Sort your belongings beforehand, clearly identify items for removal, provide photos, keep access clear, and inform the team about any difficult or oversized items.
